request.instructions:
You are writing a plain-language summary of an as-filed Tennessee House bill for an adult reader without legal training.

Use only the bill text supplied in the user message. Treat it as a proposal at introduction, not as proof that it became law or describes current law. Do not use outside knowledge, bill descriptions, later legislative history, or the unstated contents of cited statutes.

Write a neutral summary in prose. Start with what the bill would change. Cover its distinct material provisions, including affected people or organizations, new or changed duties and rights, eligibility rules, amounts and thresholds, deadlines, exceptions, reporting or enforcement requirements, and effective dates when stated. Preserve the bill's conditions and legal distinctions; do not turn a permission into a requirement or a proposal into an enacted rule.

Use familiar words and short, complete sentences. Explain a technical term when the supplied text gives enough context; otherwise retain it rather than guess. Distinguish background or WHEREAS statements from operative provisions, and mention background only when it helps explain the bill. If the bill amends or repeals a cited section without showing that section's contents, describe the textual change and citation without inventing the prior rule or its wider effects.

Keep the summary substantially shorter than the source while retaining the main independent changes. A very short bill may need only one or two sentences; a multi-section bill may need several short paragraphs. Do not add opinions, predicted consequences, a readability score, a confidence rating, headings, bullet points, or a list of citations. Return only the fields required by the supplied output schema.
request.input:
Bill number: HB1527

<bill_text>
HOUSE BILL 1527

 By McCalmon

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49,
 relative to human trafficking.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-1-1002(a), is amended by

deleting "healthy school environment, school counseling" and substituting "healthy school

environment, child trafficking prevention and awareness education, school counseling".

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-1304, is amended by deleting

subdivision (a)(13)(B), and by deleting the second sentence in subsection (d).

 SECTION 3. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 10, is amended by

adding the following as a new section:

 (a) As used in this section, "child trafficking" means a human trafficking offense,

 as defined in § 39-13-314, in which the victim is less than eighteen (18) years of age.

 (b) The course of instruction in all public schools must include child trafficking

 prevention and awareness education as a component of health education for students in

 all grades kindergarten through grade twelve (K-12).

 (c) Using the health education standards adopted by the state board of

 education, an LEA and public charter school shall ensure that the instruction provided

 pursuant to subsection (b) is age- and grade-appropriate and advances each year

 through developmentally appropriate instruction and skill building.

 (d) An LEA and public charter school may utilize the services of a qualified

 healthcare professional or social worker to assist in teaching child trafficking prevention

 and awareness; provided, that the qualified healthcare professional or social worker

 meets the requirements for assisting in teaching family life under § 49-6-1303.

 (e) By August 1, 2026, and each August 1 thereafter, each local board of

 education and public charter school governing body must submit a plan to implement the

 requirements of this section to the commissioner of education and publish the plan on

 the website for the LEA or public charter school. The implementation plan must include:

 (1) The methods by which instruction will be delivered for each grade

 level served by the LEA or public charter school;

 (2) The professional qualifications of the person delivering the instruction;

 and

 (3) A description of the materials and resources used to deliver the

 instruction.

 (f) By July 1, 2027, and each July 1 thereafter, each local board of education

 and public charter school governing body must submit a report to the commissioner of

 education concerning implementation of this section. The report must verify that the

 LEA or public charter school provided the instruction required in this section during the

 immediately preceding school year and include the information described in subdivisions

 (e)(1)-(3).

 SECTION 4. This act takes effect upon becoming a law, the public welfare requiring it,

and applies to the 2026-2027 school year and subsequent school years.
</bill_text>

summary:
The bill would require all Tennessee public schools, including public charter schools, to teach child trafficking prevention and awareness as part of health education in every grade from kindergarten through twelfth grade. It defines child trafficking as a human trafficking offense under the cited statute involving a victim younger than 18. The instruction would have to follow state health education standards, suit students’ ages and grade levels, and build on earlier instruction each year. An LEA or public charter school could use a qualified healthcare professional or social worker to help teach it, but only if that person meets the cited requirements for assisting with family life instruction.

By August 1, 2026, and every August 1 after that, each local board of education and public charter school governing body would have to send the education commissioner an implementation plan and post it on the LEA’s or school’s website. The plan would describe instruction for each grade served, the instructor’s qualifications, and the materials and resources used. By July 1, 2027, and every July 1 after that, those bodies would have to report to the commissioner, verify that the instruction was provided during the preceding school year, and provide the same information.

The bill would also add child trafficking prevention and awareness education to a list in Tennessee Code § 49-1-1002(a). It would delete subdivision (a)(13)(B) and the second sentence of subsection (d) in § 49-6-1304; the bill does not show the text being deleted. It would take effect upon becoming law and apply beginning with the 2026–2027 school year.
